assumptions: Time-independent Hermitian H0, finite-dimensional Gibbs state rho0 = exp(-beta H0)/Z, and Hermitian observables A and B independent of the applied field.

The weak perturbation is Hprime(t) = -f(t) B. The retained +i/hbar sign gives delta<A(t)> = integral dtprime chi_AB(t-tprime) f(tprime) to first order; reversing the coupling sign reverses the response.
variables: A(t) = exp(i H0 t/hbar) A exp(-i H0 t/hbar); brackets denote Tr(rho0 ...). Theta(t) is the causal step function; [A,B] = AB-BA.
chi_AB(t): retarded response kernel. chi_AB(omega) = integral from -infinity to infinity dt exp(+i omega t) chi_AB(t).
patches.regime: Hamiltonian linear response about equilibrium; not a nonlinear response or a generic reduced open-system response law. Field-dependent observables can require additional contact terms.
patches.units: hbar has energy-times-time units. chi_AB(t) has units [A][B]/(energy*time), chi_AB(omega) has [A][B]/energy, and f has energy/[B].
patches.theoryRelationship: Matches the source response R_AB in Eq. (6b), with the explicit negative perturbation-coupling convention. The source is a modern primary research paper, not the original Kubo derivation.

sourceLocations.locator: Inspected arXiv:2110.03497v3, Sec. 2, printed/PDF pp. 3-4, Eqs. (5)-(6b) and the Fourier definition after Eq. (7).

assumptions: Hermitian A in thermal equilibrium rho0 = exp(-beta H0)/Z at T > 0, with finite moments; delta A = A-<A>. This is the auto-correlation relation, not a generic cross-response formula.
Use the same Hprime(t) = -f(t) A response and +i omega t Fourier convention as the Kubo card. The spectrum is two-sided and symmetrized, not normally ordered or unsymmetrized.
variables: S_AA(omega) = (1/2) integral from -infinity to infinity dt exp(+i omega t) <delta A(t) delta A(0) + delta A(0) delta A(t)>. There is no 1/(2 pi) in this forward transform.
chi_AA(omega): retarded susceptibility; Im denotes its imaginary part. omega: angular frequency; beta = 1/(k_B T).
patches.regime: Apply the displayed coth form at nonzero frequency, including discrete spectral weights as distributions. At zero frequency use a justified regular limit; a separate elastic delta peak from nondecaying fluctuations is not recovered by naively multiplying coth(0) by zero response. Nonequilibrium states need separate relations.
patches.units: S_AA has units [A]^2*time and chi_AA(omega) has [A]^2/energy; multiplication by hbar matches units. hbar*omega/(2*k_B*T) is dimensionless.
patches.theoryRelationship: Source Eqs. (6a)-(8b), specialized to A = B = delta A and solved for the symmetrized spectrum away from zero frequency. Source C_AA maps to this card S_AA; source R_AA maps to chi_AA.

sourceLocations.locator: Inspected arXiv:2110.03497v3, Sec. 2, printed/PDF p. 4, Eqs. (6a)-(8b), Fourier convention and following A = B specialization.

assumptions: Fermionic finite-mode grand-canonical representative: Hermitian H, conserved particle number N with [H,N]=0, real chemical potential mu, K = H-mu N, and rho = exp(-beta K)/Z.
T_tau orders later imaginary times to the left and inserts a minus sign for exchanging fermionic operators. The displayed leading minus sign is the chosen modern Green-function convention.
variables: psi(tau) = exp(tau K) psi exp(-tau K); psi is a fermionic annihilation operator and psi-dagger its adjoint. Brackets denote Tr(rho ...).
beta = 1/(k_B T); Z = Tr exp(-beta K). tau is imaginary time measured in inverse-energy units.
patches.regime: T > 0 and initially 0 < tau < beta, with antiperiodic extension G(tau+beta)=-G(tau). Equal-time values require one-sided limits. This fermionic representative is not a real-time retarded propagator or a statement of bosonic ordering conventions.
patches.units: beta and tau have inverse-energy units; physical imaginary time is hbar*tau. G has the units of psi*psi-dagger, dimensionless for a normalized lattice mode.
patches.theoryRelationship: Modern imaginary-time re-expression of the source thermal ordered propagator, not a verbatim historical equation: Martin-Schwinger use a -i propagator prefactor rather than the displayed minus sign.
